parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor/Vendor)

plans.note: Liability language most likely sits with or immediately after the all-caps warranty disclaimer block in Article VIX (sec-p0109/p0112/p0116); check Article XXIV general provisions for a residual cap. Test mutuality, cap size against fees paid, and carve-outs (confidentiality, IP infringement, willful misconduct).

No indemnity heading appears in the outline; scan Article X (confidentiality) and Article XXIV general provisions before concluding it is missing. If only a Licensee-side indemnity exists, that is a deviation — we need Licensor IP-infringement and misconduct indemnity.

Licensee acknowledgements/restrictions in Article II and the non-solicitation article are the likely home of any restraint on our business; the defined term 'Right of First Refusal' also hints at a restraint. Flag only restrictions on what we may operate, buy or build.

'Right of First Refusal' is a defined term, so an exclusivity-style lock-in on future platform purchases is probably operative in Article VIII or Article II. Confirm we retain freedom to source competing FX platforms.

The per-trade fee tiers are the only pricing text visible and no MFN language is signalled. Direction rule: only flag if we are obliged to extend best terms to the Licensor; an MFN in our favour is welcome.

Article X is expressly captioned 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION'. Check whether the non-solicit binds Licensee, its duration, employee scope, and whether general advertising/unsolicited applicants are carved out.

Term/termination mechanics are likely in Article VIII (with 'Initial Period' defined in Article I) or in the general provisions. Confirm we may exit on notice without penalty and that the Licensor cannot terminate for convenience mid-term.

'Initial Period' is defined in Article I; the renewal/rollover mechanic should follow in Article VIII. Check notice window length for non-renewal and any uplift on renewal pricing (uplift cap absence is a note, not a deviation).

Governing law/venue almost certainly sits in the Article XXIV general provisions block. New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales are acceptable; foreign or mandatory arbitration is a deviation.

Look for the assignment clause in general provisions; 'AFFILIATE' is defined in Article I, so check whether affiliate/successor assignment by us is permitted without consent and whether our change of control triggers Licensor termination.

Article I defines DERIVATIVE WORK, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS and MORAL RIGHTS and Article II contains the grant and Licensee acknowledgements — the likely place for any assignment of our data, feedback or configurations to the Licensor. Direction rule: flag only transfers away from us.

Article II is the grant clause; read against the Article I definitions of FIELD OF USE, AFFILIATE, LICENSED SOFTWARE and PLATFORM SOFTWARE. Check that affiliates and our contractors are covered and that the grant is not revocable at the Licensor's discretion.

With volume-tiered per-trade pricing, a usage-verification/audit right for the Licensor is plausible in Article II restrictions or the payment article (sec-viii). Test frequency, notice, on-site scope and who bears cost.

Check the payment/Supplemental Payments provisions and fee tiers for late-payment penalties, shortfall charges or stipulated damages payable by us; ordinary interest at a commercial rate is acceptable. Credits running to us are not flagged.

Article VIX is a blanket 'WARRANTY DISCLAIMER' disclaiming merchantability, non-infringement and fitness, and stating defects may not be corrected — likely a deviation for lack of any affirmative performance warranty or remedy. Confirm no separate warranty survives elsewhere (e.g., maintenance obligations).

No insurance heading appears anywhere in the outline; sweep Article XXIV general provisions to confirm before recording as missing. Licensor hosts trading/platform data, so standard coverages (commercial general, professional/tech E&O, cyber) are expected.

The volume-banded per-trade rates plus the defined 'Supplemental Payments' and 'Market Day' terms suggest minimum volume or minimum monthly payment obligations. Check for take-or-pay/shortfall true-up and whether we have an exit.

No wind-down or data-return heading is visible; check the termination consequences in Article VIII and the confidentiality return-of-materials language in Article X, which may cover return of Confidential Information but not migration assistance.
